feedback: Missing required REWARD_FUNCTION entries for per-state else self-loops? Not here, but the fatal issue is reward semantics: transitions to u_done pay 1.0 on `at_exit`, yet the environment pays 0 when the box is not in hand at the exit. On the at_exit transition, holding_box is not guaranteed: an agent can exit right after a fall? No — at_exit and box_fell cannot coincide, so from u_carry/u_carry2 holding_box holds. However, from u_carry the agent could reach the exit having dropped the box? Not possible — drop does nothing before the first fall, so u_carry implies holding until u_fallen. Real problems: (1) no reward on `at_exit` from u_fallen/u_fallen2 — the agent can step onto the exit while the box is on the floor (the episode still ends, paid 0). Since the transition `(u_fallen, at_exit)` is not listed, the machine falls into the else self-loop and never reaches u_done; the RM should have an explicit self-loop or u_done transition with 0 reward there. As written, `at_exit` from u_fallen leaves the machine stuck in u_fallen for the rest of the (zero-length) episode — mostly harmless, but the terminal event is unmodelled. (2) The pickup reward of 0.2 combined with the fall reward of 0.1 is unbounded via cycling: falls are at most two per episode, so the net is bounded in practice — acceptable. (3) More seriously, the task says 'pick it up again on your very next move' — the machine cannot verify 'very next move' because u_fallen's else self-loop also allows delayed pickups, and the 0.2 progress reward is paid equally for late pickups. No state or reward distinguishes immediate pickup; semantic fidelity to the task's immediacy requirement is missing. (4) In episodes with only one fall, the machine handles it fine, and missing-siren setups pose no issue since siren predicates are unused — fine. (5) `box_fell & !at_exit` guard is redundant given the constraint but harmless. Verdict: reject primarily for missing at_exit handling from u_fallen/u_fallen2 (terminal step unmodelled, transition coverage incomplete) and for not enforcing the 'very next move' pickup requirement.
